title: geo.reverse_geocode
description: Reverse geocoding as ONE confirmable answer: a coordinate pair in, a PlaceResolution dict out — {lat, lon, geohash, lang, formatted, address, feature, alternatives, nearest}. This is what a consumer calls to stamp a human address onto a row it only has coordinates for, and what the browser's geolocation result resolves through. Goes through the same cache + spend ledger as the HTTP proxy.

lang.description: Requested language; clamped to the provider's indexed set. The language actually used comes back as "lang".

limit.description: Candidates to consider: the first is the pick, the rest become "alternatives".

nearest.description: Also return N nearest known Location rows from the tree (0 = do not query it at all).
